transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: On the Q2 2026 earnings call, management said net revenue rose 17% to $11.2 billion and EPS rose 20%, calling it Visa’s strongest net revenue growth since 2022 and, excluding unusual comparison periods, since 2013.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management emphasized unusually strong revenue growth in Q2 2026.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: In our fiscal second quarter, net revenue was up 17% year-over-year to $11.2 billion and EPS was up 20%. This represented the strongest net revenue growth since 2022. When you exclude the post-pandemic recovery and the Visa Europe acquisition, it was the strongest since 2013.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management reported payments volume of $3.7 trillion, up 9% constant-currency, and processed transactions of 66 billion, up 9%.
transcript_evidence.summary: Core network volume and transaction KPIs grew 9%.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Payments volume grew 9% year-over-year in constant dollars to $3.7 trillion. Processed transactions grew 9% year-over-year to 66 billion.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: CEO Ryan McInerney framed Visa as the “leading hyperscaler of payments globally” and said its Visa as a Service stack should drive future growth across consumer, commercial, money movement, AI/agentic commerce, stablecoins/blockchain, and value-added services.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management presented multiple strategic growth vectors for Visa’s platform.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Our business has incredible momentum. Visa has become the leading hyperscaler of payments globally. Our strategy and Visa as a Service stack will help us drive future growth in four important ways. One, we are winning in consumer payments, commercial payments, and money movement. Our investments and innovations are paying off in a meaningful way and will continue to drive growth.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management said AI and agentic commerce can expand Visa’s addressable market and accelerate long-term growth.
transcript_evidence.summary: Visa positioned AI and agentic commerce as a long-term growth opportunity.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Two, AI and agentic commerce will expand our addressable market and our efforts will accelerate Visa's long-term growth.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management described stablecoins and blockchain as significant opportunities and positioned Visa as an interoperability layer between new infrastructure and real-world user solutions.
transcript_evidence.summary: Visa sees blockchain and stablecoins as strategic opportunities tied to its network role.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Three, stablecoins and blockchain are significant opportunities, we've established Visa's role as a key interoperability layer between this powerful infrastructure and real-world solutions for users.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Value-added services represented 30% of Visa net revenue and were growing more than 25% in constant dollars, according to management.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management highlighted VAS as a large and fast-growing part of Visa revenue.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Four, value-added services is an even bigger opportunity and has demonstrated its value as a key driver of our growth, now representing 30% of our net revenue, growing at 25%+ in constant $.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Management said Visa has “deep conviction” in its ability to grow revenue not only over the next three to five years, but beyond.
transcript_evidence.summary: Management expressed confidence in sustained long-term revenue growth.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: We have deep conviction in our ability to grow revenue well into the future, not just for the next three to five years, but beyond.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Visa is pursuing fintech, wallet, and app partnerships, including TikTok in the U.K. and PayPay in Japan, to capture both carded and non-carded payments.
transcript_evidence.summary: Partnerships with apps and wallets are part of Visa’s strategy to expand transaction capture.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: We are winning with fintechs, wallets, and apps. They are building on our stack and tapping into our innovation and our vast acceptance footprint to help hyperscale their growth and ours, capturing both carded and non-carded payments. A few recent examples. Just last week in the U.K., we partnered with TikTok to launch a debit card specifically designed for content creators.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: In Japan, Visa is collaborating with PayPay, which management said has 40 million monthly transacting users and millions of acceptance locations, to deploy domestic and international solutions.
transcript_evidence.summary: PayPay partnership offers exposure to cash displacement and international expansion in Japan.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: In Japan, a country with nearly 50% of spending in cash, we are collaborating with mobile payments app PayPay and their 40 million monthly transacting users and millions of acceptance locations to deploy new domestic and international solutions. With Visa, PayPay plans to grow Japanese merchant acceptance, utilize our Visa Flexible Credential to integrate multiple payment methods into a single Visa credential, and expand internationally.

transcript_evidence.title: V_transcriptt.txt
transcript_evidence.claim: Commercial and money movement solutions revenue grew 24% in constant dollars, while Visa Direct had more than 18 billion endpoints and Q2 transactions rose 23% to 3.7 billion.
transcript_evidence.summary: Commercial/money movement and Visa Direct metrics showed strong growth and scale.
transcript_evidence.excerpt: Shifting to commercial and money movement solutions, where revenue grew 24% in constant dollars as we continued to reinforce the value of our offering with expanded reach and tailored solutions. Visa Direct, the largest money movement network globally, now has more than 18 billion endpoints. This vast network is helping us win new business and power more transactions. In Q2, we had 3.7 billion transactions, up 23% year-over-year.

strategic_transaction_evidence.title: 8-K exhibit: q22026earningsrelease.htm
strategic_transaction_evidence.claim: Net revenue growth was driven by higher payments volume, cross-border volume, and processed transactions; Q2 processed transactions reached 66.1 billion, up 9%.
strategic_transaction_evidence.summary: Revenue growth was underpinned by volume and transaction expansion.
strategic_transaction_evidence.excerpt: Net revenue in the fiscal second quarter was $11.2 billion, an increase of 17%, driven by the year-over-year growth in payments volume, cross-border volume and processed transactions. Net revenue increased 16% on a constant-dollar basis. Payments volume for the three months ended December 31, 2025, on which fiscal second quarter service revenue is recognized, increased 8% over the prior year on a constant-dollar basis. Payments volume for the three months ended March 31, 2026 increased 9% over the prior year on a constant-dollar basis. Cross-border volume excluding transactions within Europe, which drives our international transaction revenue, for the three months ended March 31, 2026, increased 11% on a constant-dollar basis over the prior year. Total cross-border volume on a constant-dollar basis increased 12% over the prior year. Total processed transactions, which represent transactions processed by Visa, for the three months ended March 31, 2026, were 66.1 billion, a 9% increase over the prior year.
strategic_transaction_evidence.notes: Classified as strategic transaction because merger/acquisition/divestiture/RMT/deal terms dominate the document.

strategic_transaction_evidence.summary: All listed revenue categories grew, while client incentives also increased.
strategic_transaction_evidence.excerpt: Fiscal second quarter service revenue was $5.0 billion, an increase of 13% over the prior year, and is recognized based on payments volume in the prior quarter. All other revenue categories are recognized based on current quarter activity. Data processing revenue rose 18% over the prior year to $5.5 billion. International transaction revenue grew 10% over the prior year to $3.6 billion. Other revenue of $1.3 billion rose 41% over the prior year. Client incentives were $4.2 billion, up 14% over the prior year.
